paragraphs.title: A Call to Sing and Proclaim the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Sing unto the LORD, all the earth.”
easy.q: Who is called to sing unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Sing unto the LORD, bless his name.”
easy.q: What are people told to do to the LORD’s name?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 commands God’s people to show forth his salvation from day to day.
easy.q: What should be shown forth from day to day?

medium.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Declare his glory among the heathen.”
medium.q: Among whom should the LORD’s glory be declared?

medium.explanation: “Shew forth” means to announce or make something known.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “shew forth” mean in this passage?

answers: Singing, blessing the LORD’s name, and proclaiming salvation
medium.explanation: The verses call people to sing, bless the LORD’s name, and show forth his salvation.
medium.q: Which sequence of actions appears in these verses?

answers: All the earth and all people
challenge.explanation: The call reaches all the earth, the heathen, and all people.
challenge.q: What is the scope of the call in these verses?

answers: Both help make the LORD’s glory and salvation known
challenge.explanation: The passage joins worshipful singing with declaring God’s glory, wonders, and salvation.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between singing and proclaiming?

challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that God’s salvation should be proclaimed continually.
challenge.q: What does “from day to day” emphasize?

answers: Great and greatly to be praised
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 4?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “For all the gods of the nations are idols.”
easy.q: What does the passage say about the gods of the nations?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “but the LORD made the heavens.”

answers: The gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens
The LORD is described as an idol
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the idols of the nations with the LORD, who made the heavens.
medium.q: What is the main difference between the gods of the nations and the LORD?

answers: Images or powerless objects of worship
medium.explanation: Here, idols are lifeless and powerless objects of worship, unlike the LORD.
medium.q: What does “idols” mean in this passage?

answers: Before the LORD and in his sanctuary
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.”
medium.q: Where are honor, majesty, strength, and beauty found?

answers: The idols are equal to the LORD
The LORD has power as Creator, unlike the idols
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: The passage presents idols as powerless while declaring that the LORD made the heavens.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the contrast between idols and the LORD?

answers: He is greatly to be praised and made the heavens
He dwells only in the field
He is never described as powerful
challenge.explanation: His greatness is shown by the praise due to him and by his work as Creator.
challenge.q: What supports the description of the LORD’s greatness?

answers: It is associated with strength and beauty
It is described as without holiness
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 connects the sanctuary with strength and beauty.
challenge.q: How does the sanctuary relate to the description of the LORD?

paragraphs.title: The Nations Called to Honor the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people.”
easy.q: Who is called to give glory and strength unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “bring an offering, and come into his courts.”
easy.q: What are people told to bring?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “Say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth.”
easy.q: What should be said among the heathen?

answers: An offering is brought and people come into his courts
medium.explanation: Verse 8 connects giving glory to bringing an offering and coming into the LORD’s courts.
medium.q: What happens after giving glory unto the LORD?

medium.explanation: An offering is a gift presented to honor the LORD.
medium.q: What does “an offering” mean in this passage?

answers: The world is established and the people are judged righteously
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says the world shall be established and the LORD shall judge the people righteously.
medium.q: What follows the declaration that the LORD reigns?

answers: Giving honor, bringing an offering, worshipping, and proclaiming his reign
challenge.explanation: The passage calls the nations to honor the LORD, bring an offering, worship, and proclaim that he reigns.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the nations’ response to the LORD?

answers: His reign establishes the world so that it shall not be moved
His reign causes the world to disappear
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 says, “the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved.”
challenge.q: What is the connection between the LORD’s reign and the stability of the world?

challenge.explanation: The verse says, “he shall judge the people righteously.”
challenge.q: How does verse 10 describe the LORD’s judgment?

paragraphs.title: Creation Rejoices before the Lord’s Judgment

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad.”
easy.q: What is told to rejoice and be glad?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.”

answers: All the trees of the wood
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice.”

medium.explanation: To be glad means to rejoice or be joyful.
medium.q: What does “be glad” mean in this passage?

answers: They all participate in joy and rejoicing
They are all brought as offerings
medium.explanation: The whole creation is pictured as rejoicing before the LORD.
medium.q: What do the heavens, earth, sea, field, and trees have in common?

answers: Before the LORD comes to judge
medium.explanation: The passage says creation rejoices before the LORD, who comes to judge the earth.

answers: The LORD’s reign concerns the whole world
Only human beings are connected with judgment
challenge.explanation: The heavens, earth, sea, field, and trees all respond to the LORD’s coming.
challenge.q: What does the participation of all creation in rejoicing suggest?

challenge.explanation: The LORD judges the world with righteousness and the people with his truth.
challenge.q: How is the judgment described in verses 13?

answers: His coming to judge is the reason for the rejoicing
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrase “for he cometh” connects the LORD’s coming judgment with creation’s rejoicing.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the LORD’s coming and creation’s rejoicing?
